body:
### Problem

I got here from #12409 after realizing that the help documentation for `Man` is incorrect. It states this:

```
Local mappings:
K or CTRL-]        Jump to the manpage for the <cWORD> under the cursor. Takes a count for the section.
CTRL-T               Jump back to the location that the manpage was opened from.
gO                      Show the manpage outline. |gO|
q                         :quit if invoked as $MANPAGER, otherwise :close.
```

After some investigation there seems to be a long history around what the 'q' mapping should do (quit the window but should it quit Nvim if it's the last window, previous different behaviour if invoked as $MANPAGER or not).

From what I can tell, the current behaviour is an unconditional mapping to always quit. From `runtime/ftplugin/man.vim`:
```lua
if !exists('g:no_plugin_maps') && !exists('g:no_man_maps')
  nnoremap <silent> <buffer> j             gj
  nnoremap <silent> <buffer> k             gk
  nnoremap <silent> <buffer> gO            :lua require'man'.show_toc()<CR>
  nnoremap <silent> <buffer> <2-LeftMouse> :Man<CR>
  nnoremap <silent> <buffer> <nowait> q :lclose<CR><C-W>q
endif
```

I think the behaviour should be no map when nvim is not invoked as $MANPAGER. This was also discussed in pull #12483 [here](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/12483#issuecomment-643773802).
However, #12483 didn't end up going through and instead was fixed by #18443 which always keeps the mapping (changes between `:lclose<CR><C-W>q` and `:lclose<CR><C-W>c`, but the mapping is always created).

Unfortunately, it looks like v0.11 got rid of `vim.g.pager`, so I'm not sure how to detect if in pager mode. Only method I could find was to check for the existence of $MAN_PN that `man` sets when spawning the pager, e.g.
```lua
  if exists('$MAN_PN')
    nnoremap <silent> <buffer> <nowait> q :lclose<CR><C-W>q
```
However I think $MAN_PN is man-db only. I think the better fix is just to reintroduce `vim.g.pager` (or rename it to something like `vim.g.manpager`) in `runtime/lua/man.lua:init_pager()` (just before the `set_options()` call, as before) and then have something like the following diff:
```
diff --git a/runtime/ftplugin/man.vim b/runtime/ftplugin/man.vim
index 5ea36c32ce..fea7392f3d 100644
--- a/runtime/ftplugin/man.vim
+++ b/runtime/ftplugin/man.vim
@@ -26,7 +26,9 @@ if !exists('g:no_plugin_maps') && !exists('g:no_man_maps')
   nnoremap <silent> <buffer> k             gk
   nnoremap <silent> <buffer> gO            :lua require'man'.show_toc()<CR>
   nnoremap <silent> <buffer> <2-LeftMouse> :Man<CR>
-  nnoremap <silent> <buffer> <nowait> q :lclose<CR><C-W>q
+  if get(g:, 'man_pager')
+    nnoremap <silent> <buffer> <nowait> q :lclose<CR><C-W>q
+  endif
 endif
 
 if get(g:, 'ft_man_folding_enable', 0)
diff --git a/runtime/lua/man.lua b/runtime/lua/man.lua
index ac1bc8eee0..79fa57e721 100644
--- a/runtime/lua/man.lua
+++ b/runtime/lua/man.lua
@@ -709,6 +709,7 @@ function M.init_pager()
     vim.cmd.file({ man_bufname, mods = { silent = true } })
   end
 
+  vim.g.man_pager = true
   set_options()
   vim.bo.bufhidden = 'unload'
 end
```


### Expected behavior

As mentioned in a [comment](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/12483#issuecomment-643773802) on #12483, the 'q' mapping should be removed when not being used as a pager, to stay consistent with other behaviour (e.g. help windows) and not surprise the user (me)

Documentation needs to be updated to reflect current behaviour since 'q' never behaves as `:close` anymore and (currently) closes neovim if the man window is the last window

comment_data.body: This would be another case where `<Plug>(nvim-closewin)` could avoid revisiting this topic over and over https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/31706
